J1.evidence: Ḥassān verse «ومِنَّا الذي لاقى بسيفِ محمدٍ ... فجاسَ به الأعداءُ عَرْضَ العساكرِ»: the source vocalises «الأعداءُ» in the nominative (the enemies as subject), but EN 'and with it ransacked the enemies' silently treats it as accusative object (الأعداءَ), i.e. translates a different text without a Translator's note; EN also inserts '[the foe]' after 'met' as a plain bracket, an addition not in the Arabic and not inside [Translator's note: …]. The prose part of EN (وعد four views, عباد/عبيد, جاسوا meanings, خلال) is otherwise faithful and complete. Fix: mark '[the foe]' as Translator's note and render/annotate the verse per the written vocalisation.

J2.evidence: Hassan verse in the source reads «فجاسَ به الأعداءُ» with الأعداءُ nominative (subject); EN 'with it ransacked the enemies' treats it as an accusative object, i.e. translates a differently vocalised text without a note. EN also adds unmarked '[the foe]' to «لاقى بسيفِ محمدٍ». Both need a Translator's note (vocalisation as written / bracket addition).

en.fixed_note: Hassan verse: '[the foe]' put inside Translator's note; الأعداءُ now rendered as subject per the written nominative ('the enemies ranged'), with a Translator's note on the vocalisation

J1.evidence: Labīd's verse «جِنٌّ لدى بابِ الحصيرِ قيامُ» is glossed 'at the door of the king's enclosure'; the Arabic says only بابِ الحصيرِ; 'king's' (an interpretive gloss of الحصير as the king) is not in the text and not inside [Translator's note: …], and it even obscures why the author cites the verse (for «الحَصِيْرُ: الحَبْسُ», prison). Unmarked addition; fix by e.g. 'the door of al-ḥaṣīr' with any gloss in a Translator's note. Rest of EN faithful.

J2.evidence: Verse is cited for «الحَصِيْرُ: الحَبْسُ»; «لدى بابِ الحصيرِ» is rendered 'at the door of the king's enclosure' - 'king's' (and 'enclosure') is an interpretive gloss not in the Arabic and unmarked; should be 'al-Ḥaṣīr' / prison with any king gloss inside a Translator's note.

en.fixed_note: Labid verse: unmarked 'king's enclosure' replaced by literal 'al-ḥaṣīr'; gloss moved into Translator's note
